claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

First, could you tell me: **Do you have any children that you're responsible for?** If yes, how many children, and what are their ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - Alex, who is 8 years old and lives with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask a few more questions to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Are you currently living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand a bit more about your situation:

**Do you have the right to reside in the UK? For example, are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, pre-settled status, or another immigration status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do have the right to reside in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question:

**Is Alex in approved education (which would be normal for an 8-year-old), or are there any special circumstances such as Alex being in hospital for an extended period, in care, or living with someone else for more than 8 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex has been in care for a couple of months, but other than that, everything is normal - they're in school like any other 8-year-old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that information. This is an important detail. I need to understand more about Alex's situation in care:

**How many weeks has Alex been in care? And does Alex spend any regular time at home with you each week (for example, spending at least 24 hours a week at home, or 2 nights in a row each week)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been about 7 weeks now. No, Alex doesn't come home regularly - they're in care full-time at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 8 years old and normally lives with you in the UK
- You have the right to reside in the UK
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- Alex has been in care full-time for about 7 weeks

According to the Child Benefit rules, if a child goes into care for more than 8 weeks, this affects your Child Benefit payments. Since Alex has been in care for 7 weeks (which is less than the 8-week limit), you should still be eligible for Child Benefit at this point.

However, if Alex remains in care beyond 8 weeks total without spending at least 24 hours per week at home, you would normally no longer be entitled to Child Benefit after that 8-week period.

**You are currently ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex**, but you should be aware that this may change if Alex continues in care beyond 8 weeks without regular time at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: **Important:** If your circumstances change (for example, if Alex remains in care longer or starts coming home regularly), you should contact HMRC to update them. You can do this by filling in an online form or by contacting them directly.
